reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) discusses magneto-dielectric coupling and bulk magnetic order in Nd-HEO films, not FeMnNiGeSi-type HEAs, and does not address microstrain, defects, domain wall pinning, or annealing effects on magnetocaloric response. E3 compares annealed and as-rolled bulk HEAs but does not link microstrain or domain wall pinning to magnetocaloric broadening or hysteresis. None of the key premises are supported by the provided passages.
premises: As-deposited FeMnNiGeSi-type HEA nanoscale films/ribbons have high internal microstrain, defect density, and compositional heterogeneities.
These microstructural features cause spatial variations in magnetic exchange and enhanced domain wall pinning.
Enhanced domain wall pinning broadens the magnetocaloric entropy change profile and increases hysteresis.
Thermal annealing relieves internal stresses and reduces nanoscale defects.
Reduced domain wall pinning after annealing yields a sharper, more pronounced magnetocaloric response with lower hysteresis.
